chunks: He said: 'Inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, He said: 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you disclose and what you conceal?'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Adam being asked to name the angels in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this event establishes the concept of 'Ilm al-Ghayb' (Knowledge of the Unseen) as a divine attribute shared by the Prophets and Imams, positioning Adam as the first bearer of this sacred knowledge. The naming of the angels serves as a tangible proof of Adam's intellectual superiority, validating his role as God's vicegerent (Khalifah) on Earth. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and intellectual hierarchy established by God, where knowledge precedes physical creation.
